messages.subject: legends question
parts:
I have a working plot, that plots a data frame (histogram) in
navy/white, a mean in goldenrod and another data frame in red.

I would like to add some form of heading, somewhere, saying
something like

All Queries
Mean
Spam Queries

in the corresponding color (or reasonable approximation).

Any ideas?

A pointer to a URL or vignette will do just fine, of course, but
working solutions would be appreciated :-)-O


require(scales)
require(ggplot2)

qplot(data=allqueriesDF,
x = as.Date(Date),
y = Queries,
xlab = "Date",
ylab = "Queries") +
scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
theme_bw() +
geom_bar(stat = "identity",
fill = "navy",
color = "white") +
geom_line(data=spamqueriesDF,
aes(x=as.Date(Date), y=Queries),
color = "red", size=2) +
geom_line(data=allqueriesDF,
aes(x=as.Date(Date), y=mean(Queries)),
color = "goldenrod", size=2)

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: legends question
parts:
If you used a line plot instead of a bar chart, this would be fairly
easy: map color in each layer to a named factor level and use
scale_color_manual() to set the colors. For example,

qplot(data=allqueriesDF,
x = as.Date(Date),
y = Queries,
xlab = "Date",
ylab = "Queries") +
scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
theme_bw() +

geom_line(aes(color = "All queries"), size = 2) +
geom_line(data=spamqueriesDF,
aes(x=as.Date(Date), y=Queries,
color = "Spam queries"), size=2) +
geom_line(data=allqueriesDF,
aes(x=as.Date(Date), y=mean(Queries),
color = "Mean"), size=2) +
scale_color_manual(values = c("blue", "red", "goldenrod")) +
labs(color = "Type")

If you insist on keeping the bar chart, you have a problem because
blue is set to fill whereas red and goldenrod are set to color. You
could use blue for the color aesthetic in the bar chart and then it
would work by substituting the aes(color = "All queries") part into
geom_bar(). I prefer three lines (same information, less ink), but
YMMV.

Dennis

Dennis,

thank you very much.

What I ended up doing was splitting the graph into 2, one for the
histogram, because I can demonstrate something interesting, that in
our small ccTLD the DNS queries reduce over the weekend.

I have the smoothed the lines so they look prettier in the very
small sample which shows the reduction in queries after I mentioned
the words "Stoererhaftung" and "Beihilfe" to the hoster,
"Urheberrechtsverletzung" to the abuser, and "Staatsanwalt" to both
:-)-O

I'll continue to collect the data until the day before the presentation
so I get more data.

I am genuinely impressed, and have ordered the Wickham book from Amazon.

el
